In [[set theory]],  '''Jensen's covering theorem''' states  that if [[zero sharp|0<sup>#</sup>]] does not exist then every [[uncountable]] set of [[Ordinal number|ordinal]]s is contained in a [[constructible universe|constructible set]] of the same [[cardinality]]. Informally this conclusion says that the [[constructible universe]] is close to the universe of all sets. The first proof appeared in {{harv|Devlin|Jensen|1975}}. [[Jack Silver|Silver]] later gave a fine-structure-free proof using his [[Silver machine|machines]]<ref>W. Mitchell, [https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Inner-Models-for-Large-Cardinals-Mitchell/ecf7380a4468e233a23282157b318e20156e3a1a Inner models for large cardinals] (2012, p.16). Accessed 2022-12-08.</ref> and finally  {{harvs|txt|authorlink=Menachem Magidor|last=Magidor|year=1990}} gave an even simpler proof.

The converse of Jensen's covering theorem is also true: if 0<sup>#</sup> exists then the countable set of all cardinals less than <math>\aleph_\omega</math> cannot be covered by a constructible set of cardinality less than <math>\aleph_\omega</math>.

In his book ''Proper Forcing'', [[Saharon Shelah|Shelah]] proved a strong form of Jensen's covering lemma.

[[Hugh Woodin]] states it as:<ref>"In search of Ultimate-L" Version: January 30, 2017</ref>
:Theorem 3.33 (Jensen). One of the following holds.
::(1) Suppose λ is a singular cardinal. Then λ is singular in L and its successor cardinal is its successor cardinal in L.
::(2) Every uncountable cardinal is inaccessible in L.
